resources.string: One place to launch your games, watch how your phone is doing, and set up each game the way you like.
Every number comes from Android itself. When a reading is not available on your phone, Game Master says so instead of guessing.
Some features need special access, such as drawing over other apps. Next you can review each one and grant only what you want.
Implemented, not yet tested on a device
This screen only exists as a navigation target. Nothing on it is simulated. It will be built in phase %1$d.
Detect installed games, search, sort and filter them, add games manually, hide games without uninstalling, and launch them.
Show one game\'s information, recent sessions and a shortcut to its own settings.
Balanced, Performance, Battery saver and Custom modes with settings that are applied when a game starts and restored when it ends.
Frame rate and frame-time history with average, minimum and maximum, using only methods Android supports. Methods that need root will be labelled.
Do Not Disturb, brightness and volume controls, screenshot and screen recording shortcuts, gaming timer and session statistics.
A draggable overlay with live readings and quick actions while a game is running. It needs the Display over other apps permission.
Connection type, Wi-Fi details, signal, latency and ping tests, and speed history. Measured latency is not the same as in-game ping, and the app will say so.
Total playtime, sessions, most played games and daily, weekly and monthly activity, stored on this device.
An independent profile for each game: preferred mode, brightness, Do Not Disturb, overlay and monitoring layout.
Only real device readings are shown here. Features that are not built yet are labelled instead of simulated.
CPU load, GPU readings and thermal sensors are not built yet. They are planned for phase 4 and will only appear when Android provides real data.
Game Master asks for access only for features that need it. Every permission is optional, and you can change them later in Settings.
Lets Game Master tell which game is in the foreground, so it can track play sessions and apply per-game settings.
Needed for the floating game panel and the FPS overlay while a game is running.
Android requires a visible notification for the service that keeps the overlay and monitoring running.
Lets Game Master silence interruptions while you play and restore your previous setting afterwards.
This settings page could not be opened on your device.
Stops the screen from turning off while Game Master is open.
Review and change the access Game Master has.
Game Master follows your system language, English or Indonesian. On Android 13 and newer you can also set it for this app in system settings.
A gaming assistant that shows real device readings and sets up each game your way.

This is an early build. Game library, game modes, FPS monitor, overlay, network tools and statistics are not built yet. Android does not let ordinary apps change CPU or GPU frequency, so Game Master will never claim to.
